blocks.content: The tectonic plates are in constant motion relative to each other, driven by convection currents deep within the Earth's mantle.

items: Distinguish plate boundaries: Divergent creates crust, Convergent destroys crust, and Transform conserves crust.
Identify major versus minor plates: Cocos, Nazca, Arabian, Philippine, and Caroline are frequently tested minor plates.
San Andreas Fault is the most classic example of a transform plate boundary.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Earth's rigid lithosphere is divided into 7 major and several minor plates that float upon the semi-fluid asthenosphere.
Divergent boundaries pull plates apart, allowing upwelling magma to form new crust at mid-ocean ridges.
Convergent boundaries occur where plates collide, giving rise to mountain ranges, deep sea trenches, and volcanic arcs through subduction.
Transform boundaries involve plates sliding horizontally past one another, conserving landmass while generating frequent seismic activity.
Thermal convection currents operating within the upper mantle act as the main mechanism propelling plate movements.
